name: The Quanta Ceiling: Tier Mobility Is Algorithmic Theater
description: Widespread belief holds that HelixCore Corporation's proprietary TierScore algorithm — the system used by every corponation to assess upward mobility eligibility — is deliberately tuned to prevent net population movement above Tier 2. Believers cite the 2209 leak of an internal HelixCore memo, nicknamed the 'Flatline Document,' which allegedly shows TierScore recalibrates annually to maintain a fixed social distribution curve. The memo's authenticity has never been confirmed, but its language — 'demographic stability protocols' and 'aspirational pressure valves' — has become street gospel in the Gray Zone. Some economists in Tier 3 quietly acknowledge the math doesn't support the mobility rates HelixCore advertises.
cultural_impact: the Gray Zone communities have largely abandoned formal TierScore improvement programs, redirecting energy into ghost markets and informal economies as genuine alternatives to corporate mobility ladders. The phrase 'chasing your score' has become the Gray Zone slang for naïve futility.
locations: The Stacking District, Lower the Gray Zone
Varga's Pressure Drop bar, Tier 2 Cuyahoga Corridor
story_hooks: A Tier 2 data analyst discovers her own TierScore has been manually flagged — not by algorithm, but by a human administrator she's never met.
The original whistleblower who leaked the Flatline Document resurfaces, claiming the real document was far worse and that the leak itself was a controlled burn to discredit the truth.
A player character is offered a genuine Tier 3 slot by a HelixCore fixer — but accepting it requires them to publicly denounce Priya Osei-Tanaka.
believers: Tier 1 and Tier 2 residents, underground economists, the Gray Zone art collectives, anti-corporate activists
evidence: The Flatline Document exists and circulates on the Underworld; independent statistical analysis shows mobility rates 60% below HelixCore's published figures. However, the algorithm is not fully static — exceptions exist, likely to maintain plausible deniability.
